subtopic: Deciding whether to join a protest
passage: Sunday night. The signature march for the library fund is over and I'm too wired to sleep, so I'm writing. What I learned: the organisers kept to the route, and a volunteer with a whistle kept the lines neat. I hadn't known that most of it is waiting. What felt bad: when a stranger began shouting at people on the pavement, my stomach dropped and I moved next to Jahnavi ma'am. Did it work? Honestly, maybe forty people watched. But the councillor's assistant took our letter, and that's something. I'm not sure I'm the shouting type. Tomorrow I'll ask Jahnavi ma'am how to join the school committee so I can help plan things like this properly. Small steps. — Ira

qa.q: What did Ira feel when the stranger began shouting?
qa.a: Uneasy: Ira's stomach dropped and Ira moved closer to Jahnavi ma'am.

qa.q: How else could Ira stay involved, and why might it work?
qa.a: Ira could write to the councillor or help make posters, since these suit Ira's comfort with noise; the committee also lets Ira help plan events carefully.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi ma'am see Ira asking about the committee?
qa.a: Jahnavi ma'am, who stood beside Ira during the uncomfortable moment, would likely see a student who thought through the day and wants to take part responsibly.

grounding: After a peaceful gathering a teen reviews what was learned, what was uncomfortable and how effective it was, and chooses the school committee.

Zainab: home from the park thing. that was intense
Disha: the tree-cutting protest? how was it
Zainab: peaceful. like 300 people. mostly families and old people
Zainab: I thought it'd feel powerful but mostly I felt awkward holding a sign
Disha: 😅 why
Zainab: I didn't know half the facts people were shouting. felt fake
Disha: did it do anything tho
Zainab: a councillor came and listened for 10 min. said they'd review
Zainab: idk if that means anything
Disha: so was it worth it?
Zainab: kind of? I learned a lot from this retired botanist uncle. he knew every tree
Zainab: but honestly I think the school eco committee could do more, long term
Disha: you're joining?
Zainab: applying tomorrow. and I'm reading about the park plan tonight so I'm not clueless next time
Disha: proud of you 🙂

qa.q: How many people were at the protest?
qa.a: Like 300 people, mostly families and old people.

qa.q: How did Zainab feel holding the sign?
qa.a: Zainab felt awkward and a bit fake, not knowing half the facts being shouted.

qa.q: What else could Zainab do to be better prepared next time?
qa.a: Zainab could read the park plan and talk to the botanist or the eco committee before any event, so every sign held is understood.

qa.q: How does Zainab's decision look to Disha?
qa.a: Disha seems proud and pleased, seeing Zainab turn a mixed experience into a longer-term commitment.

grounding: A chat shows a teen reviewing a peaceful protest, what was learned, what felt uncomfortable and how effective it was, then deciding to join a school committee.

passage:
The walk to the block office in Barwani had been peaceful: about eighty villagers, mostly farmers, asking for the canal water to be released on time. Eshaan, sixteen, had gone with his uncle and his friend Wasim.

That night, on the charpai under the neem tree, Eshaan couldn't sleep. He kept going over the day. What had he learned? That the canal schedule was set in the district, not the block. That the older farmers knew exact dates and numbers, and he knew nothing. What had felt uncomfortable? Shouting slogans he hadn't chosen. And had it worked? The officer took their paper and promised to forward it. That was all.

Next morning he told Wasim, "I want to keep going, but not only marches. The school has a youth committee that writes to the panchayat. I'm joining that."

Wasim grinned. "You'll be the one with the numbers next time."

qa.q: How many villagers took part in the walk?
How did Eshaan feel lying awake that night?
qa.a: He felt restless and thoughtful, a bit uneasy about shouting slogans he hadn't chosen and unsure whether the walk had achieved much.

qa.q: What else could Eshaan do on the youth committee to make a difference?
qa.a: He could collect the canal dates and numbers from the older farmers, so the committee's letters to the panchayat are specific.

qa.q: How might Wasim see Eshaan's new plan?
qa.a: Wasim seems encouraging and amused, expecting Eshaan to become the one who knows the numbers.

grounding: Shows a teen reviewing what was learned, what felt uncomfortable and how effective a peaceful gathering was, then deciding to stay involved through a committee.
